subject: OrbitalPay - Performance instrument and termination rights (SLA redlines)
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@orbitalpay.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@orbitalpay.com
Date: 2026-09-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: OrbitalPay SLA redlines - fees at risk and termination

Tessa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement reviewed the draft SOW and SLA and we have a substantive request that we need to resolve before we can move forward with the pilot. High level: we need a cash-backed performance instrument tied to severe/repeat P1 latency incidents and explicit termination rights if the service is not materially remediated.

What OrbitalPay is proposing:
- A performance bond or escrow equal to 3 months of committed MRR (to be held with an independent agent) as security for repeated P1/P2 failures.
- A termination right for OrbitalPay if there are 3 P1 incidents within any 90-day rolling window and Redwood fails to restore performance within a 30-day cure period.
- The ability to require an independent forensic audit after any P1 that results in data exposure or >30% SLA degradation.

We attach our redlines (orbital_sla_redlines_v1.docx) and a brief incident history showing why we need a cash instrument (incident_history_orbital.xlsx). This is a non-negotiable procurement requirement for regulated payments partners — credits alone do not satisfy compliance.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can post an insurer-backed bond or accept a third-party escrow? If not, we need to understand Redwood's alternative that provides equivalent commercial protections.

Regards,
Emily Zhao
Head of Procurement, OrbitalPay
From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@orbitalpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitalPay SLA redlines - fees at risk and termination

Emily — thanks for the context and the files. I appreciate the clarity around procurement constraints and the regulatory angle.

Quick response: Redwood understands the need for strong commercial protections for payment platforms. Historically, we avoid posting cash-backed bonds tied to customer revenue because that model shifts financial risk to the platform in a way that is hard to price and insure. That said, there are several practical, market-standard alternatives we can explore that get you a similar risk posture without Redwood carrying open cash liability on our balance sheet. Examples include:
- An insurer-backed performance bond (issued by an accepted A-rated insurer), which we are open to discussing — would need insurer details and standard terms.
- A mutually-agreed escrow arrangement where a neutral escrow agent holds a reserve funded by either Redwood or a monthly reserve created from invoice credits (hybrid approach).
- Defined, tiered financial remedies (credits + capped cash payout tied to severity and repeat incidents) with explicit cure windows and an independent auditor clause.

I'll loop in our legal lead to draft a considered counterproposal that preserves your regulatory protections while keeping a commercially sustainable structure for Redwood. Are you available for a call Thursday morning (9/11) to walk through the acceptable insurer/escrow options?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@orbitalpay.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@orbitalpay.com
Date: 2026-09-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitalPay SLA redlines - fees at risk and termination

Tessa —
We can be flexible on the mechanics, but the commercial effect must be the same: a cash-backed instrument available for drawdown in the event of repeat, unremediated P1s. Our compliance team will not accept a pure-credit-only remedy because of reconciliation and capital reserve rules.

If Redwood can get an insurer-backed instrument, we need a short list (3) of insurers and sample policy terms (limits, exclusions, notice requirements). If Redwood prefers an escrow, it must be a true third-party escrow agent with funds accessible to OrbitalPay upon trigger and governed by a simple release schedule tied to severity/repeat definitions.

We are preparing suggested language to make this concrete and will send by EOD. We are also sensitive to timeline — our go-live is targeted for 2026-11-01, so we need to close commercial terms this month.

—Emily
From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@orbitalpay.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitalPay SLA redlines - fees at risk and termination

Emily / Tessa — looping in legal. Thanks for the specifics, Emily. We took a look and prepared a proposed counter that aims to balance OrbitalPay's compliance needs with Redwood's commercial constraints. See attached: counter_sla_terms_redwood.docx (high level summary below).

Redwood counter (high level):
- Performance reserve: 60-day reserve (equal to ~2 months' committed MRR) that is funded from monthly invoices by withholding a portion of credits into a neutral escrow account administered by a mutually-agreed escrow agent. This keeps Redwood from having to post cash up-front while giving OrbitalPay access to a fund on trigger.
- P1 repeat/termination: termination right only after 4 P1 incidents in a 180-day rolling window *and* failure to remediate within 30 days after written notice. This raises the bar slightly (4 incidents/180 vs 3/90) while preserving termination as a last-resort remedy.
- Independent audit: allow a neutral third-party auditor to conduct a post-incident review for material incidents. If audit finds Redwood non-compliant with SLA, escrow funds become payable per schedule. Audit scope and auditor selection to be mutually agreed; timing limited to preserve operational security.
- Cap: overall cash exposure capped at the reserve amount (no open-ended liquidated damages).

Rationale: this structure provides a tangible, accessible reserve for the customer while keeping Redwood's open cash liability and insurer negotiation complexity contained. If OrbitalPay requires an insurer bond instead, we can explore that route but will need time to engage our broker and confirm terms/availability.

Tessa / Marissa — please advise on technical acceptance criteria language (definitions of P1, measurement windows, what constitutes remediation). Emily — do you and procurement have flexibility on the incident counts/window and on the escrow-vs-bond mechanics?

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Trevor Lim <trevor.lim@orbitalpay.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@orbitalpay.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitalPay SLA redlines - fees at risk and termination

Rafael — thanks for the thoughtful counter. A few notes from OrbitalPay legal/procurement:

- We are open to a reserve funded from monthly credits only if the reserve is funded by Redwood (not by reducing OrbitalPay's access to invoice credits). In other words, the reserve cannot diminish OrbitalPay's liquidity.
- If Redwood cannot post a direct cash-backed bond, we will accept an insurer-backed performance bond. Please provide a list of acceptable insurers and sample policies. We will need the insurer to be A-rated and to commit to prompt payment on validated draws.
- The termination condition in your counter (4 P1s / 180 days) is materially different than our ask. We can consider 3 P1s / 120 days as a compromise, provided the cure window remains 30 days.

We understand these are operationally difficult asks; however, this is standard for regulated payments integrations. Given our November go-live, we need to converge this week.

—Trevor Lim
Sr. Legal Counsel, OrbitalPay
From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@orbitalpay.com>, Trevor Lim <trevor.lim@orbitalpay.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitalPay SLA redlines - fees at risk and termination

Thanks all — summary and Redwood's commercial offer below so we can get to a DocuSign-ready position. Quoting the key commitments only; full legal language to follow.

Redwood offer (final commercial position):
1) Performance reserve: Redwood will establish a 60-day performance reserve (approx. 2 months' committed MRR). The reserve will be held in a neutral escrow administered by a mutually agreed agent. Initial funding: Redwood will seed the reserve (cash) on contract execution and then top-ups, if needed, will follow the documented schedule tied to incident draws. This avoids reducing OrbitalPay's invoice credits while providing you with a cash-accessible instrument.
2) Termination trigger: OrbitalPay will have termination rights after 3 P1 incidents within a 120-day rolling window *and* Redwood fails to restore agreed performance within a 30-day cure period following written notice. This aligns with your ask and Trevor's compromise.
3) Independent audit: OrbitalPay may request a neutral third-party post-incident review for any P1 that meets the materiality threshold. Auditor selection will be by mutual agreement; audit findings that confirm SLA breach will permit escrow draw per the release schedule.
4) Cap: Redwood's total cash exposure is capped at the funded reserve. Any payout reduces the reserve; replenishment mechanics to be agreed (Redwood commits to replenish to a floor within 90 days if payouts occur).

Next steps: Rafael will circulate formal contract language and a draft DocuSign packet by EOD 9/17. Please confirm your acceptance of the high-level commercial structure and provide any final insurer names if you still prefer an insurer-backed bond instead of the seeded escrow. DocuSign link will be shared once legal language is agreed.

Onwards — can we take 30 minutes tomorrow to finalize? Proposed times: 9/17 08:30 PT or 9/17 11:00 PT.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
